run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-18T01:59:58Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend coincides with a fault applied to the shipping→quote hop. From 01:58:00Z to at least 02:08:00Z, Chaos Mesh created a new NetworkChaos experiment every minute (Schedule otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition, namespace chaos-mesh) and each one applied chaos to pods otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and otel-demo/quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b / quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt for ~55s before TimeUp/Recovered. Frontend's checkout path began recording error spans between 01:59:00Z and 01:59:30Z (the checkout error counter was flat at 44 from 01:52:00Z through 01:59:00Z and the 5-minute error increase was 0 in every window ending 01:42–01:59) and stayed at roughly 79% error spans for /api/checkout through 02:08Z. The same window shows shipping's own /get-quote server spans and POST quote client spans erroring at the same magnitude, checkout's PlaceOrder erroring, quote's span volume collapsing from ~450–490 per 5m to ~57–101 per 5m, and shipping logs holding 22 queued 'Requesting quote' lines with no 'Sending Quote'/'Tracking ID Created' until the experiment's TimeUp at 02:05:55Z. Pods were all Running/ready with 0 restarts, endpoints existed for shipping and quote, and all flagd fault flags are 'off', so a pod failure, restart/rollout, missing endpoint or feature-flag fault is not supported. Conclusion is partial because the fault objects themselves (chaos Schedule/NetworkChaos custom resources) are only visible through Kubernetes events and their specs could not be read, and the first experiment (01:58:00Z) did not visibly raise errors until ~01:59Z.

claims.text: Frontend's checkout error counter (traces_span_metrics_calls_total, service_name=frontend, span_name='POST /api/checkout', status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, SPAN_KIND_SERVER) held the value 44 at every 30s sample from 01:52:00Z to 01:59:00Z, then read 71 at 01:59:30Z, 132 at 02:00:30Z, 184 at 02:03:30Z and 237 at 02:05:30Z, so error spans began between 01:59:00Z and 01:59:30Z.

The 5-minute increase of error spans for service_name=frontend was 0 at every point from 01:42:00Z through 01:59:00Z and became non-zero at 02:00:00Z (121.46) and 02:01:00Z (235.56), confirming the alerting signal deviated only around 01:59Z.

At the 02:08:00Z instant, over the preceding 5 minutes, span increases by status for span_name='POST /api/checkout' were STATUS_CODE_ERROR 127.08 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 33.74 on frontend; the same magnitudes appear on frontend's other checkout spans (POST, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder).

In the same 02:03–02:08Z window service shipping recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR 123.71 vs STATUS_CODE_UNSET 33.74 on both '/get-quote' (server) and 'POST quote' (client), and service checkout recorded STATUS_CODE_ERROR 124.84 vs STATUS_CODE_UNSET 33.74 on 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder'; these are span counts, not request counts.

Frontend operations outside the checkout path recorded no error-span increase in 02:03–02:08Z: 'GET /api/cart', 'GET /api/data', 'POST /api/cart', 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', grpc CartService/GetCart and AddItem and grpc AdService/GetAds all returned 0.

Service quote's 5-minute span increase fell from 456.7/473.3/480/432.1/490 at 01:50–01:58Z to 170 at 02:02Z, 56.7 at 02:04Z, 73.3 at 02:06Z and 101.2 at 02:08Z, and the only status_code value present on quote's span series in this window is STATUS_CODE_UNSET.

Events show Schedule otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh reporting 'Create new object: otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition-<suffix>' at 01:58:00Z, 01:59:00Z, 02:00:00Z, 02:01:00Z, 02:02:00Z, 02:03:00Z, 02:04:00Z, 02:05:00Z, 02:06:00Z, 02:07:00Z and 02:08:00Z.

Each spawned NetworkChaos (names otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition-nh2wt, -wg96t, -w588w, -r952x, -x4hvd, -m59h5, -sq968, -2c44x, -8h4xd, -xb6sh, -kx8th) reports 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9', '...quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b' and '...quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt', then 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos' about 55s later; PodNetworkChaos 'Updated' events for those same three pods recur every 30–60s across 01:58–02:08Z.

Shipping pod shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 logs during the 02:05:00–02:05:55Z experiment show 22 'Requesting quote' lines (02:05:26.55–02:05:54.28Z) with no 'Sending Quote' or 'Tracking ID Created' until 02:05:55.17Z, after which four quotes completed within ~0.75s; in the gap between experiments (02:05:58.57Z and 02:05:59.38Z) 'Requesting quote' was followed by 'Sending Quote' and 'Tracking ID Created' within ~50ms.

All 22 otel-demo pods were Running and ready with 0 restarts and start times 01:23:48–01:25:48Z, including frontend-675fd7b5c5-d2vwq, checkout-5dccddf8bb-vz2zd, shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 and both quote pods (quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b, quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt).

Endpoints objects exist for service quote with two pod addresses (100.96.2.155 quote-6b5877698d-x9hwt, 100.96.4.53 quote-6b5877698d-sdl5b on port 8080) and for service shipping with one pod address (100.96.4.227 shipping-75d58f5d84-6xkt9 on port 8080).

Every fault flag in ConfigMap flagd-config (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) is ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', so no flagd-injected shipping/quote/checkout fault is switched on.

Quote service failing on its own is not supported: quote's span series carry only STATUS_CODE_UNSET in this window, its pods were Running/ready with 0 restarts, and its request volume fell rather than erroring, so the failure sits on the shipping→quote call path, not in quote's own error handling.

A pod restart, crash or rollout of frontend/checkout/shipping/quote is not supported: those pods have restartCount 0, start times 01:23:48–01:23:50Z (before the incident) and there are no SuccessfulDelete events for otel-demo pods.

The other activity in the window (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, Job SuccessfulCreate/Completed, StatefulSet SuccessfulCreate, PVC provisioning and PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete, all in namespace data-recorders) is not tied to this alert: every one of those events involves data-recorders objects, while the frontend errors come from the otel-demo checkout path.

The Chaos Mesh network-partition experiments between shipping and quote are the mechanism behind the frontend alert: shipping's 'Requesting quote' calls hang while a NetworkChaos experiment is active and complete immediately once it recovers, quote's inbound volume collapses at the same time, shipping's /get-quote and POST quote spans error, checkout's PlaceOrder inherits the failure, and frontend's POST /api/checkout returns ~79% error spans; the shared timing and target pods make the partition the best-supported cause, but the causal link is inferred from timing plus events, not from a readable chaos spec.

Advisory: inspect and, if this partition is not intentional, suspend/delete the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh and its spawned NetworkChaos objects, then confirm that shipping→quote calls and frontend /api/checkout error spans return to the pre-01:59Z baseline of zero error increase.

gaps: The fault objects are Chaos Mesh custom resources (kind NetworkChaos and kind Schedule in namespace chaos-mesh); those kinds are not readable with the available Kubernetes tools, so the partition's action, direction, duration and target selector could not be verified directly and are known only from event messages and object names.

No change-history integration is available, so when the Schedule was created or when the partition was switched on cannot be established; only that its first spawned experiment in this window is at 01:58:00Z.

The first experiment started at 01:58:00Z, but frontend checkout error spans first appear between 01:59:00Z and 01:59:30Z (and quote volume was still normal in the 5m window ending 02:00Z); the ~1 minute offset between the first applied chaos and the first errors is unexplained.
Frontend pod logs (frontend-675fd7b5c5-d2vwq) returned 0 bytes / 0 lines for 01:55–02:09Z, so no application error text for /api/checkout could be read.
Checkout pod logs (checkout-5dccddf8bb-vz2zd) had no lines matching error/failed/unavailable/DEADLINE/quote among 659 lines read, so no app-side error text was observed there either.

Jaeger returned no traces for any query window after ~01:44Z (frontend 01:59:30–02:01Z and 02:03–02:04Z, shipping 02:08–02:15Z all empty), so the checkout→shipping→quote edge could not be confirmed from trace parent references during the incident.

kube-state-metrics series such as kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned nothing for 01:37–02:15Z, so deployment-level readiness could not be checked from Prometheus and the pods query was used instead.
Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas in namespace otel-demo returned no objects; that empty result only shows the query matched nothing and does not by itself prove they are absent.
The span-metric series used for the error counts end at 02:08:58Z, so frontend/shipping error behaviour and the state of the Schedule after that time are unknown.

The alert's own 1.111 error-rate value could not be reproduced from an identifiable Prometheus rule: no rule named RequestErrorRate (and no rules at all) were returned by list_prometheus_rules for this target.
next_steps: Read the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-shipping-quote-network-partition and its NetworkChaos objects in namespace chaos-mesh to confirm action (partition), direction, and target pods.
Identify who created the Schedule (chaos workflow/CI/operator) and whether the experiment is expected to keep running every minute.
Collect frontend container logs and, once available, Jaeger traces from the incident window to confirm the failing checkout→shipping→quote chain at span level.
After any change, compare frontend POST /api/checkout and shipping /get-quote STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases against the pre-01:59Z baseline of zero.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
